cards.text: Friend, this is John's first letter to believers, and it's not a story. It's one point stacked on top of another, like a tower of cookies, and if you pull one out the whole thing wobbles. Point one: everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God.

cards.question: Think family here. John says whoever loves the Father also loves who else?

answers.text: The prophets who spoke for Him

cards.text: Then John runs it backward, and the first time I read it I had to sit down, which is TOUGH when you're stuck standing on a gold base. He explains how we can tell we really love God's children.

cards.question: So how does John say we can tell we really love the children of God?

answers.text: When we love God and keep His commandments
When we never argue with one another
When we give away all we own

cards.text: Loving God, John says, means keeping His commandments. And before anybody groans like I do when the oven timer goes off in the MIDDLE of my nap, John has something to say about those commandments.

cards.question: True or false: John says God's commandments are a heavy burden.
God's commandments aren't burdensome. What reason does John give?

answers.text: Everyone born of God overcomes the world
God only gives a handful of them
Most of them were meant for priests

cards.question: Overcoming the world takes a victory. John says the victory that has overcome the world is our ___.

cards.text: Then John asks it out loud, like the announcer at a baking contest holding up the trophy: "Who then overcomes the world?" I LOVE when John asks a question, friend, because he never leaves you hanging.

cards.question: True or false: John says the one who overcomes the world is whoever believes that Jesus is the Son of God.

cards.text: Now John points right at Jesus, the One who came by water. Then John underlines it the way I underline "TOP RACK" three times on every recipe card: not by water alone.

cards.question: Not by water alone. What else does John say Jesus came by?

cards.text: And John says Someone testifies to all this, and it's not some rumor from the group chat. It's Someone John calls the truth.

cards.question: Who does John say testifies that Jesus came by water and blood?

cards.text: Then John lines up his witnesses like it's a courtroom. He says there are three that testify.

cards.question: John's three witnesses are the Spirit, the ___ and the ___.
True or false: John says the Spirit, the water and the blood disagree with each other.

cards.text: John says we accept human testimony. Friend, the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with swore EVERY day they still had a little charge left, and I believed them EVERY time.

cards.question: Compared to human testimony, what does John say about the testimony of God?

cards.text: John says whoever believes in the Son of God has this testimony within him. Not on a sticky note, not in a drawer somewhere, but inside.

cards.question: Whoever doesn't believe the testimony God gave about His Son, John says, has made God out to be a ___.

cards.text: So what exactly is the testimony God has given about His Son? John spells it out, and friend, I'd frame this one and hang it right over the ovens.

cards.question: According to God's testimony, what has God given us?
John says this eternal life is in God's ___.

cards.text: Then John says it plain: whoever has the Son has life. I spent years in a junk drawer thinking my story was over, and it turns out life was never about the drawer.

cards.question: True or false: John says whoever does not have the Son of God still has life.

findings.problem: The card says the letter was written 'to believers.' That fact comes from 1 John 5:13, which is outside the passage, but the card cites only 1 John 5:1 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Every card says 'John says.' The text of 1 John never names its author. The docs allow saying who wrote a letter 'with their reference,' but this letter has no verse that names its writer.
findings.question: When a letter doesn't name its author in its own text, like 1 John, may Papa Dorin call the writer 'John' based on the book's name? Or should he use a neutral wording, like 'the writer' or 'the letter'?

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Everyone born of God overcomes the world,' uses Bible wording. The wrong answers are casual and modern: 'God only gives a handful of them' and 'Most of them were meant for priests.' The right answer also reasons about the believer, while both wrong answers reason about the commandments themselves, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'He never leaves you hanging' claims that John always answers his own questions. That isn't true across the letter. For example, 1 John 3:17 asks 'how can the love of God abide in him?' and gives no answer.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The setup for card 4 capitalizes 'Someone' twice, which marks the witness as divine. That rules out the wrong answers 'The angels' and 'The prophets' before the question is asked.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'John says we accept human testimony' turns the BSB's conditional, 'Even if we accept human testimony,' into a flat statement. The 'if' is dropped.

'It turns out life was never about the drawer' is unclear. A baker can't tell how the drawer connects to having the Son and having life. It doesn't land as a joke either, and a stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
